in_arabic.name: أقيبن
in_arabic.meaning: أقيبن النبي يُقَبَّلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُقَبَّلٌ
in_arabic.long_meaning: أَقِيبَنَ في اللغة العربية يُقَبَّلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُقَبَّلٌ، وَيُشَكَّلُ مِن القَبولِ، وهو اسم فاعل من أَقَبَّلَ، وَهُوَ مِن قَبَلَ، وَالقَبولُ مَعناهُ الرِضا وَالسَلامُ، وَكَذَلِكَ أَقِيبَنَ مُقَبَّلٌ، وَيُشَكِّلُ مِن قَبَلِ وَالقَبولِ، وَهُوَ أَصَحُ مِن مُعَرَّدِ المُقَبَّلِ، وَهُوَ مَقَبولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ، وَهُوَ مُقَبَلٌ عَلَيْهِ، وَهَذَا الاسم مِنَ الأَسْماءِ الَّتِي يَجْمَعُ مَعَها النَبيّ صَلَى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَيّامَ المَبْعَثِ، وَهُوَ مِنَ الأَسْماءِ الَّتِي يُشَكِّلُ مِنَ الرِضا وَالتَسَلُّمِ، وَالجَماعَةُ بِاللَهِ وَحِدَهُ، وَهَذَا الاسم يُكتبُ بِاللُغَةِ الْحَرَمِيَّةِ، وَهُوَ مَذْهَبُ المُحَدِثينَ، وَهُوَ يُكتبُ بِاللُغَةِ الْعَامِيَّةِ، وَهَذَا مَذْهَبُ أَكثَرِ النَاسِ

In Islamic tradition, aqibun is a name that is associated with the prophet Muhammad, who was accepted by Allah after going on Allah's path and being pleased with him. The name aqibun is also associated with the concept of acceptance and approval, which is a central theme in Islamic theology. In modern times, the name aqibun is used in various Muslim cultures to signify acceptance and approval from Allah.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Aqibun" is believed to have originated from the Arabic language and is not commonly used among Muslims, making it a unique and distinctive name. It is significant in the Islamic culture as it symbolizes the importance of being punctual and prompt in all aspects of life, especially in fulfilling religious obligations such as prayer and fasting. The name is also a reminder of the Prophet Muhammad's saying, "The early is dear to Allah and His Messenger" (Bukhari and Muslim), emphasizing the significance of being ahead of time and preparing for the future.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Aqibun" holds great significance in the Islamic faith as it signifies being present and attentive in the moment. It is a reminder of the Prophet Muhammad's saying, "The most beloved things to Allah are the most consistent in good deeds" (Bukhari and Muslim). By striving to be "the one who comes before" or "the one who is early," the bearer of this name is encouraged to prioritize their spiritual growth and connection to Allah, seeking His pleasure and favor. Additionally, the name "Aqibun" can serve as a reminder of a hadith stating, "Part of a person's being steadfast is depending on Allah," emphasizing the importance of reliance on Allah in all aspects of life (Tirmidhi). Together, these interpretations highlight the significance of being present, prepared, and reliant on Allah in order to lead a virtuous and spiritually fulfilling life.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Vol. 9, p. 217-218. The name Aqibun carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Aqibun Ibn Usayd Al-Khudri was one of the Ten Promised Paradise (Ashab Al-Ash'arah). He participated in the Battle of Khaybar, led by Muhammad (PBUH), and later in the Battle of Hunain. He was given the title Aqibun due to his bravery and his position at the end of the ranks of the Muhajirun (emigrants).

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Sa'd, Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra, Vol. 2, p. 444-445. The name Aqibun carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Aqibun Ibn Usayd Al-Khudri was appointed as the Governor of Egypt by Caliph Umar bin Al-Khattab. He ruled Egypt for two years and was known for his fair administration and justice. During his rule, he led an expedition against the Byzantines and was successful in conquering the areas around Dishmash and Dumyat. He was later succeeded by Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas as the Governor of Egypt.
